beats.spoken_words: Before you scroll,
beats.visual_description: Protagonist in dark green hoodie lies propped up on bed in evening. Smartphone beams sharp cool electric-blue glow onto his face. A hand-drawn hand reaches up with a stop gesture in foreground.

beats.spoken_words: dopamine is not the pleasure chemical you think it is.
beats.visual_description: Clean educational blackboard graphic on warm cream paper. Crisp vector brain cutaway on left. On right, chemical flask filled with bubbling gold liquid labeled [ PLEASURE? ], violently slashed with Crimson Red NO.

beats.spoken_words: You think it makes you feel happy, but it doesn't.
beats.visual_description: Extreme close-up on protagonist face. Eyes wide and tired, mouth completely flat and unsmiling. Floating beside his cheek is a yellow smiley bubble struck out with a thick Crimson Red X.

beats.spoken_words: If dopamine was pleasure, you would feel satisfied after scrolling for two hours.
beats.visual_description: Side view of protagonist slumped on couch. Fast-forward motion arcs: on wall behind him, round wall clock spins wildly from 11:00 PM to 1:00 AM. Ghosted phone video cards float around him.

beats.spoken_words: Instead, you feel completely empty, foggy, and exhausted.
beats.visual_description: Protagonist hunched over edge of mattress, shoulders collapsed, eyes half-lidded with dark exhaustion circles. Above head floats a battery icon with blinking red rim reading [ 1% ].

beats.spoken_words: Neuroscientists proved this decades ago:
beats.visual_description: Vintage green chalkboard on cream paper. Cartoon stickman scientist wearing round glasses and lab coat stands beside retro anatomical brain diagram, pointing with wooden stick.

beats.spoken_words: dopamine doesn't spike when you get a reward.
beats.visual_description: Wrapped cardboard gift box with yellow ribbon labeled [ REWARD ] sits open on table. Below it on timeline axis, dopamine line is completely flat and lifeless: FLATLINE.

beats.spoken_words: It spikes right before—during the anticipation.
beats.visual_description: Stickman mitten hand hovers 2 inches above closed box, trembling. At this exact millimeter before touching box, violent Crimson Red graph spike surges up labeled [ ANTICIPATION! ] with sparks.

beats.spoken_words: It is not satisfaction. It is an itch.
beats.visual_description: Cutaway of protagonist head. Inside brain, dozens of red comic prickle lines and exclamation points vibrate like an unbearable rash. Large bold text: THE ITCH.

beats.spoken_words: A biological itch that whispers:
beats.visual_description: Close side-profile of protagonist. Looming behind his shoulder in dark is a shadowy stick figure with mischievous grin and red outlined eyes whispering into his ear: *pssst...*.

beats.spoken_words: just one more video, just one more click, maybe the next one is better.
beats.visual_description: Protagonist running frantically on revolving circular treadmill. Dangling from fishing rod strapped to his back is a glowing golden YouTube Short play button hovering inches from fingers.

beats.spoken_words: Every time you refresh, your brain floods with craving, not fulfillment.
beats.visual_description: Tight close-up of cartoon thumb pulling down on phone screen. Loading spinner turns. Sharp crimson arrows flood into cartoon brain labeled [ CRAVING ], while satisfaction gauge reads zero.

beats.spoken_words: Cheap apps hijacked this ancient hunting reflex,
beats.visual_description: Vertical split panel: Left: Ancient caveman in animal pelt tracking mammoth prints with spear. Right: Modern stickman in green hoodie hunched over glowing smartphone tracking red notification badges.

beats.spoken_words: turning your focus into a slot machine in your pocket.
beats.visual_description: Giant smartphone standing upright like Vegas slot machine. Mechanical red lever snaps down. Screen reels spin with blur, settling on [ 🔔 ] [ ❤️ ] [ 💬 ]. Protagonist stands hypnotized by lights.

beats.spoken_words: Here’s how you take control.
beats.visual_description: Medium shot protagonist turning away from phone, standing upright, arms crossed calmly, eyes focused and determined. Morning sunlight begins to cut through minimalist room.

beats.spoken_words: Put twenty seconds of friction between you and cheap dopamine.
beats.visual_description: High-impact card on cream paper: Bold Emerald Green stopwatch shield labeled [ 20 SECONDS ] stands like physical barrier between stickman and phone. Text: THE FRICTION PROTOCOL.

beats.spoken_words: Put the phone in another room,
beats.visual_description: Protagonist places black phone face-down on wooden desk in empty bedroom, then walks through doorway into hallway, leaving device behind.

beats.spoken_words: take ten deep breaths, and let the craving burn out.
beats.visual_description: Tranquil shot: Protagonist stands by open window with soft morning sunlight pouring over him. Chest expanded in deep inhale. Above head, tiny red cartoon flame gently fizzles out into white smoke.

beats.spoken_words: Real power isn't feeding the itch every five seconds—
beats.visual_description: Wide street scene: Crowd of pale stickmen walking like zombies, heads tilted down at glowing blue screens. In center, protagonist stands still, looking up with clarity and peace.

beats.spoken_words: it's having the strength to sit in stillness the second...
beats.visual_description: Centered tranquil shot on cream paper. Protagonist sits serenely on wooden bench, hands folded in lap, eyes closed in stillness. Subtle golden halo behind head. Holds quietly into loop point.
